name: Financial Services (GLBA, SOX, DORA)
description: Financial services overlay for agents handling customer financial data, transaction records, or financial reporting information. Packages evidence for GLBA Safeguards Rule controls, SOX internal-control obligations, and DORA operational resilience requirements.

evidence_requirements: Information security program documented and approved by senior leadership per GLBA 16 CFR 314.4(a)
Board or senior management oversight of information security program demonstrated (GLBA 314.4(a))
Qualified individual designated to oversee, implement, and enforce the information security program (GLBA 314.4(a))
Annual written report to the board on the information security program (GLBA 314.4(i))
SOX CEO/CFO certifications (§302) and management internal controls report (§404) address information security program
Roles and responsibilities for information security program defined and documented per GLBA 314.4(a)
Reporting structure for qualified individual with board-level accountability established (GLBA 314.4(a))
Internal audit committee independence requirements met per SOX §301
DORA management body member(s) responsible for ICT risk identified where DORA applies
Risk assessment conducted covering customer information and relevant systems per GLBA 314.4(b)
Risks to confidentiality, integrity, and availability of customer financial information identified and assessed
SOX §404 management assessment of internal controls over financial reporting documented
Risk assessment updated at minimum annually or upon material changes (GLBA 314.4(b))
Oversight mechanisms for automated financial decisions documented per SOX §302 CEO/CFO accountability
Human review required for material financial judgments made by or with agent assistance
GLBA change management oversight process includes management approval for modifications to financial systems (GLBA 314.4(g))
DORA anomaly management with management escalation path documented where DORA applies (DORA Art.15)
Inventory of systems, applications, and data assets handling customer financial information maintained per GLBA 314.4(c)(2)
Asset inventory supports scope determination for information security program controls
SOX-relevant systems identified and included in ICFR scope per §404
Software and model inventory maintained for systems processing customer financial information (GLBA 314.4(f))
Service provider and vendor software components tracked with version and approval status
Authorized software list verified as part of GLBA service provider oversight program (GLBA 314.4(f))
Customer financial information classified per GLBA categories (nonpublic personal information) per GLBA 314.4(c)(2)
Data classification scheme identifies financial data, transaction records, and financial reporting information
Classification informs controls selection per GLBA information security program requirements
Service provider oversight program documented per GLBA 314.4(f) covering selection and monitoring
Written agreements with service providers protecting customer information adequately (GLBA 314.4(f))
Periodic assessment of service providers information security practices (GLBA 314.4(f))
ICT third-party risk management per DORA Arts. 28-30 where DORA applies — register of ICT third-party arrangements maintained
Risk assessment identifies foreseeable internal and external risks to customer information per GLBA 314.4(b)
Risk assessment covers all areas of operations handling customer financial information (GLBA 314.4(b))
Agent AI system risks assessed as part of information security risk management
Access controls and multi-factor authentication enforced for systems handling customer financial information
Quarterly user access review with management sign-off for financially relevant systems
Identity and authentication controls documented in the ICT risk management program
Least-privilege entitlements and segregation-of-duties matrix maintained for finance-sensitive workflows
Provisioning and de-provisioning approvals tied to financial reporting responsibilities
Periodic scope and entitlement recertification recorded for audit review
Change management records demonstrate secure development and testing for systems processing financial data
Third-party and externally developed tool risk reviews completed before production use
Release approvals link provenance checks to control-owner accountability
Encryption protects customer financial information in transit and at rest, with compensating-control approval documented when needed
Data exposure scans cover outbound payloads, generated output, and ingested context for financial information
Cryptographic key management and transport security settings reviewed as part of financial-system control testing
Tamper-evident audit logs capture every financially relevant agent action with enough detail for ICFR review
Audit-retention schedule preserves evidence for seven years in support of SOX §802 recordkeeping obligations
Logging and monitoring controls detect unauthorized access to customer financial information
Configuration management procedures cover systems processing customer financial information (GLBA 314.4(c)(7))
Baseline configurations established for financially relevant systems with deviation detection
Patch management applied to GLBA-in-scope systems with documented timelines for critical vulnerabilities
Encryption policy covers customer financial information at rest and in transit (GLBA 314.4(c)(3))
Cryptographic key management procedures documented including key rotation and revocation
Encryption standards reviewed and updated as part of annual information security program review
Input validation and injection controls implemented for systems processing customer financial data (GLBA 314.4(c)(6))
Vulnerability management covers systems in GLBA information security program scope
Security testing of externally developed and modified applications accessing financial information (GLBA 314.4(c)(6))
Behavioral monitoring and anomaly detection cover privileged access, transaction spikes, and exfiltration indicators
Incident response plan defines triage, escalation, remediation, and reporting workflows for security events affecting financial data
Major ICT incident assessment and regulator-reporting runbooks maintained for financial-entity use cases
DE-01.framework_reference: GLBA 16 CFR 314.4(c)(8), 314.4(h); SOX §404; DORA Art.10, Art.17, Art.19

evidence_requirements: Configuration monitoring detects unauthorized changes to GLBA-in-scope systems (GLBA 314.4(d))
Alerts generated for configuration deviations on financially relevant systems
Monitoring scope verified against asset inventory of customer-information-handling systems (GLBA 314.4(d))
DE-02.framework_reference: GLBA 16 CFR 314.4(d); SOX §404; DORA Art.9, Art.15

evidence_requirements: Continuous monitoring of information security controls per GLBA 314.4(d) ongoing oversight requirement
Annual testing of safeguards including penetration testing or vulnerability assessments (GLBA 314.4(d))
Monitoring results reported to qualified individual and board per GLBA 314.4(i)
DE-03.framework_reference: GLBA 16 CFR 314.4(d); SOX §404; DORA Art.11, Art.15

evidence_requirements: Audit log integrity protected to prevent tampering — required for SOX §802 electronic record integrity
Log availability and completeness verified as part of GLBA safeguard testing (GLBA 314.4(d))
Tamper detection mechanisms in place for audit records covering financially relevant systems
Incident response plan documented per GLBA 314.4(h) covering detection, response, and recovery
Plan includes procedures for notifying customers and regulators of incidents involving customer financial information
FTC Safeguards Rule notification to Board within 30 days of events affecting 500+ customers (16 CFR 314.4(j))
Escalation and notification procedures for security incidents involving customer financial information (GLBA 314.4(h))
Board notification within 30 days of qualifying events per GLBA 314.4(j) and FTC Safeguards Rule
SOX §302/§404 management certification process includes identification of material weaknesses
External auditor notification of material control failures per SOX audit committee requirements
Incident documentation and evidence preservation procedures per GLBA 314.4(h)(5)-(6)
Records of security events and responses retained for minimum SOX §802 recordkeeping period (7 years)
Chain of custody maintained for forensic evidence from financially relevant security incidents
Business continuity and disaster recovery plan documented per GLBA 314.4(g) and 314.4(h)
Recovery procedures tested at minimum annually covering systems handling customer financial information
Recovery time and recovery point objectives defined for GLBA-in-scope financial systems
DORA Art.12 backup and recovery requirements met for EU financial entities
Post-incident review process documented per GLBA 314.4(g) including lessons learned
Lessons learned from security incidents incorporated into information security program updates (GLBA 314.4(g))
SOX management assessment updated to reflect material control improvements following incidents

reporting_obligations.assessment_type: Combined financial-services control package: GLBA Safeguards oversight, SOX internal-control evidence, and DORA operational resilience / ICT incident reporting support.
reporting_obligations.reporting_entity: Board or equivalent governing body, audit committee and external auditor, plus applicable financial regulators or competent authorities.

human_oversight_mandates.description: No explicit AI-specific oversight mandate is imposed by this combined profile, but GLBA requires a qualified individual and board reporting, SOX requires management and audit committee oversight of internal controls, and DORA assigns accountability to the management body.

DE-01.regulatory_citation: GLBA 16 CFR 314.4(h); SOX §404; DORA Art.17, Art.19

notes: This overlay treats financial-services handling as a combined control package rather than a single-regulation attestation. GLBA Safeguards Rule drives customer-information security controls, SOX drives internal-control and record-retention rigor for financially relevant systems, and DORA adds ICT resilience and incident-management expectations for regulated financial entities.
